HM-SITE-01.metaTitle: Hermit: the open-source AI agent that lives on your phone
HM-SITE-01.metaDescription: Hermit is an open-source AI agent for Android. The model runs on your phone, your memories stay there encrypted, and nothing leaves without your OK.
HM-SITE-01.lede: Hermit is an open-source AI agent that lives on your Android phone. The model runs on the phone itself, your memories stay there encrypted, and nothing leaves without your OK.
HM-SITE-01.mascotAlt: Hermit, a hermit crab, peeking out of its shell and waving
HM-SITE-01.storesNote: Not in the stores yet. A preview APK for Android is on GitHub Releases.
HM-SITE-01.doesTitle: Real work, done on your phone.
HM-SITE-01.doesIntro: Hermit is pre-alpha. The first list already works in the code. The second is still being built.
HM-SITE-01.chatBody: Talk to it in English or Spanish. The model answers from your phone, even in airplane mode.
HM-SITE-01.memoryBody: Tell it what to remember. It keeps it encrypted on the phone and forgets it when you ask.
HM-SITE-01.remindersBody: Ask in your own words. The reminder arrives on time, with no server in between.
HM-SITE-01.calendarBody: Reads your agenda and adds events to the calendar already on your phone.
HM-SITE-01.whatsappBody: Reads new messages from your notifications and drafts replies. Nothing is sent until you approve it.
HM-SITE-01.mailBody: Reads and summarizes your inbox, talking straight to your mail provider. Sending takes your fingerprint.
HM-SITE-01.vaultBody: Keeps your logins in an encrypted vault and fills them into other apps after your fingerprint.
HM-SITE-01.walletBody: Practice payments with test money on a test network. Every payment waits for your fingerprint.
HM-SITE-01.botsBody: Several bots, each with its own job and permissions, with Hermit coordinating them.
HM-SITE-01.routinesBody: Tasks that run on a schedule, under the same rules as everything else.
HM-SITE-01.companionBody: A companion on a computer you own, for the tasks too heavy for a phone.
HM-SITE-01.privateIntro: A hermit crab carries its home and keeps to itself. So does Hermit. These are its rules, and they are written into the code.
HM-SITE-01.promiseLocalTitle: The model runs on your phone.
HM-SITE-01.promiseLocalBody: What you say is processed on the device, not in a data center.
HM-SITE-01.promiseMemoryTitle: Memories stay encrypted on the device.
HM-SITE-01.promiseMemoryBody: Chats, memories and reminders live in an encrypted database on your phone.
HM-SITE-01.promiseOkBody: Anything sent for you waits for your answer, with the exact text and where it goes.
HM-SITE-01.promiseFingerBody: Sending, paying and logging in each need your fingerprint, for that exact action.
HM-SITE-01.promiseTelemetryBody: No analytics, no crash reports, no ads and no account. The build fails if a tracker is ever added.
HM-SITE-01.promiseOpenTitle: Open source, so anyone can check.
HM-SITE-01.promiseOpenBody: Every rule on this page is in the code, under Apache 2.0.
HM-SITE-01.phoneCaption: An example: before a message goes out, Hermit shows the exact text and waits for your fingerprint.
HM-SITE-01.phoneAsk: Tell Marta I'm running 10 minutes late.
HM-SITE-01.phoneReply: Here it is. It goes out only after you approve it.
HM-SITE-01.blockedAlt: Hermit tucked into its shell, claws shut over the door
HM-SITE-01.blockedBody: If something isn't allowed, Hermit tucks into its shell and shuts the door with its claws, like a real hermit crab. Then it tells you what it blocked, and why.
HM-SITE-01.harnessIntro: Every run used the same small model, {model}, on the same tasks with the same scoring. Only the harness changed: the code around the model that gives it a menu of skills, routes each request and checks each answer.
HM-SITE-01.chartSr: {from} of {total} with the generic setup, {to} of {total} with Hermit's harness.
HM-SITE-01.chartNote: Each score counts the tasks done right in its set. The blind set was written separately and scored before anyone read it. Sets of 40 tasks are small: a score can move about 15 points from one run to the next.
HM-SITE-01.tableToggle: Show the numbers as a table
HM-SITE-01.statFirstNote: Median time, on a Galaxy S26 Ultra.
HM-SITE-01.sourceBody: Hermit is open source under Apache 2.0. The cage that checks every action, the privacy checks that fail the build, the evals and this website all live in one public repository.
HM-SITE-01.sourceCodeLabel: Get the code and run the privacy checks
HM-SITE-01.labTitle: Help us make Hermit fast on every phone.
HM-SITE-01.labBody: Hermit runs a small model on the phone itself, and every phone is different. Run the benchmark on yours and share the report. Each one shows where Hermit needs work.
HM-SITE-01.labStep1Body: It times the model on your phone and checks its answers.
HM-SITE-01.labStep2Body: Nothing leaves your phone on its own. You see the report before anyone else does.
HM-SITE-01.labStep3Body: Add it to the repository, the way the guide explains.
HM-SITE-01.labNeeds: Any phone with Android 13 or later and a 64-bit ARM processor can help.
HM-SITE-01.labAlt: Hermit holding up a phone, its new home
HM-SITE-01.getBody: Hermit is pre-alpha and not in the stores yet. Preview APKs for Android are on GitHub Releases: install one, run the Device lab and file your phone's report. Star the repository to follow along, or build it from the source.

HM-SITE-02.metaDescription: Hermit collects nothing. This page lists every connection the Hermit app can make, and why.
HM-SITE-02.title: Privacy policy
HM-SITE-02.short1: Hermit collects nothing. It has no accounts, no analytics, no crash reporting, no ads and no trackers.
HM-SITE-02.short2: Dojo Coding, which builds Hermit, does not receive or process your personal data. Your data lives on your phone.
HM-SITE-02.short3: Hermit only connects to the outside world for the reasons listed below, and anything sent in your name waits for your fingerprint.
HM-SITE-02.phoneBody: Your chats, memories, reminders, the messages Hermit reads from your notifications, saved logins and the signed activity log are stored on the phone in an encrypted database. The AI model runs on the phone too, so what you say to Hermit is processed there.
HM-SITE-02.phoneContacts: Contacts are read only to find a person you name. They never leave the phone and are not stored in Hermit's database.
HM-SITE-02.phoneCodes: Android hides one-time sign-in codes from apps like Hermit, and Hermit hides any that arrive in your messages: it never stores them. One exception: in a web task, if the site asks you for a code, Hermit shows you the message it came in (Android asks your permission for that one SMS) and you decide whether to use it. It types it after your fingerprint and doesn't store it.
HM-SITE-02.connectionsTitle: Every connection the app can make
HM-SITE-02.connectionsIntro: These are all the places the Hermit app can connect to. Each request is counted on the phone, and Settings, Privacy shows every server contacted, with how many times. Only the server's name is kept, never what was asked.
HM-SITE-02.connModelWhere: Hugging Face ({hosts}) and the download servers it redirects to
HM-SITE-02.connModelWhen: Once per model version. Hermit asks for a fixed file and checks it against a pinned SHA-256 before using it. Nothing about you is sent.
HM-SITE-02.connSearchWhere: DuckDuckGo ({hosts}) by default, a SearXNG server you choose, or nothing if you turn search off
HM-SITE-02.connSearchWhen: When you ask for current facts. Only your search words are sent, and the first search in each chat asks you first.
HM-SITE-02.connWebWhere: The address you or your chat name
HM-SITE-02.connWebWhen: When you ask Hermit to read a page. Hermit fetches that page's text over HTTPS; the site sees a normal request from your phone. If the page asks for a payment and you approve it with your fingerprint, the site also gets that signed test payment.
HM-SITE-02.connMailWhere: Gmail ({googleHosts}), Outlook ({microsoftHosts}), or your own provider's mail servers
HM-SITE-02.connMailWhen: Only if you connect an account. Mail goes straight between the phone and your provider. Sending asks for your fingerprint.
HM-SITE-02.connServicesWhere: Only the ones you connect: Google Calendar and Drive, Outlook Calendar and OneDrive, Spotify, GitHub, Notion and Slack ({hosts})
HM-SITE-02.connServicesWhen: Hermit shows each service's servers before you connect. Sign-in uses the provider's own page, and the access it grants stays on the phone.
HM-SITE-02.connMcpWhere: The server you add: an address you enter, or a service's official server that Hermit suggests
HM-SITE-02.connMcpWhen: Only after you add a server. Each call to it asks for your approval.
HM-SITE-02.connRelayWhere: A relay you run (Dojo Coding's relay isn't available yet)
HM-SITE-02.connRelayWhen: Off by default. A few services need a relay to finish signing in. If you turn one on, it swaps a one-time sign-in code for your access, sends that access back encrypted to your phone, and stores nothing.
HM-SITE-02.connWalletWhen: When Hermit reads the wallet's balance or history, which sends the wallet's public address, and when you send a test payment you approved with your fingerprint.
HM-SITE-02.othersTitle: What other apps send, not Hermit
HM-SITE-02.othersWhatsapp: WhatsApp replies you approve are sent by WhatsApp. Hermit hands the reply to the notification on your phone.
HM-SITE-02.othersCalendar: Calendar events sync wherever your calendar account already syncs.
HM-SITE-02.othersApps: When Hermit opens another app for you with a prefilled message or link, that app decides what it sends.
HM-SITE-02.walletBody: Hermit has a testnet wallet for trying out payments. It works only on Stable's test network, with test money that has no real value. Its keys are made on your phone and stay there, encrypted, and using them takes your fingerprint. Every payment shows you the amount and who gets it, and waits for your fingerprint. Nothing about the wallet is sent to Dojo Coding. Settings, Delete everything erases its keys with the rest of Hermit's data.
HM-SITE-02.permissionsIntro: Each permission is asked with a reason, and each one is optional.
HM-SITE-02.permNotifications: Notification access, to read messages from the apps you allow and to reply through them
HM-SITE-02.permCalendar: Calendar, to read and add events
HM-SITE-02.permContacts: Contacts (optional), to find a person you name
HM-SITE-02.permAlarms: Notifications, exact alarms and starting after a restart, so reminders arrive on time
HM-SITE-02.permBackground: Running in the background, for the night shift while the phone charges
HM-SITE-02.permBiometric: Fingerprint or face, to approve actions and unlock saved logins
HM-SITE-02.permAutofill: Autofill service (only if you choose Hermit), to fill saved logins in other apps
HM-SITE-02.permInternet: Internet, for the connections listed above
HM-SITE-02.permNever: Hermit does not ask for SMS, location, storage or microphone access.
HM-SITE-02.deleteBody: Settings, Delete everything erases Hermit's data on the phone, and uninstalling Hermit removes it too. Sign-ins are deleted from the phone; to revoke Hermit's access at a service, remove it in that service's account settings.
HM-SITE-02.limitsBody: Hermit protects your data on a phone that is working as designed. It can't protect it on a rooted phone or against a compromised operating system.
HM-SITE-02.siteBody: This site sets no cookies and runs no analytics or third-party scripts; its fonts and images are served from the site itself. The company that hosts it may keep standard technical logs, such as IP addresses, to deliver and protect the site. If you pick the light or dark theme, your browser remembers that choice on your device and never sends it anywhere.
HM-SITE-02.downloadsBody: When you download Hermit from GitHub, GitHub's privacy policy applies to the download.
HM-SITE-02.contactPending: Write to privacy@dojocoding.io for any question about this policy or about your data. Hermit keeps your data on your phone, so we can't look it up or delete it for you: Settings, Delete everything erases it all.
HM-SITE-02.changesBody: When this policy changes, the date at the top changes with it.

HM-SITE-03.needs: For Android 13 or later, on a 64-bit ARM processor. The AI model downloads once, after you install.
